name: חֵלֹן
summary: The father of Eliab, the leader of Zebulun in the wilderness, named only as “Eliab son of Helon” when Israel was numbered, encamped, brought its offerings and set out from Sinai (Num 1:9; 2:7; 7:24, 29; 10:16). The name is חֵל, the form חַיִל takes before a suffix or another word (חֵילוֹ “his army”, חֵיל “strength of”), with the ending ־ֹן that forms names and adjectives: “strong, one of strength”. Its ē is that of חֵיל, not the ō of חוֹל “sand”, which the place Holon, חֹלוֹן, may take.

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab son of חֵלוֹן, spelled here with ו.
חֵילוֹ, “his army”: חַיִל with ē before a suffix, the vowel of the name.
בְּרֹב חֵילוֹ, by its great strength.
“Yahweh the Lord is חֵילִי, my strength.”

note: Root decided between חיל “strength” and חוֹל “sand” by the vowel: the name has ṣere (חֵלֹן, Num 10:16 חֵלוֹן), as חַיִל has in its bound forms (חֵיל, חֵילוֹ) and the rampart חֵל, while חוֹל has ō. The database keys the name under חול with the rest of the root, so root is חול and entry chayil. It could also be read from חֵל “rampart”, “of the rampart”; recorded in the gloss only as strength. The ending ־ֹן is read as forming a name or adjective, as in שִׁמְשׁוֹן from שֶׁמֶשׁ.
